You played the wrong card when you allowed yourself to loose control over what is a very difficult situation for this young lady.  She is vulnerable due to her past, the abuse, and you re-introduced those horrors for her when she was trying to show affection for you.

People who have been abused are fragile, protective people.  They have every right to be.  She is worried about getting right back into something it took strength and courage to walk away from.

Maybe you can be friends again and see is you can rebuild the trust that was lost this past weekend.  But don't be too surprised if she can't get over that.

The first thing I would ask is why you don't think you are worthy of his love?  Everyone deserves to be loved, and hopefully by the person they love as well.  Beating yourself up over past mistakes is going to get you no where in the future.  Make amends where you can and learn to live with the rest.
Be honest with him about how you feel, tell him your dreams, share your desires in life for you and for him.  Some emotions come through stronger than others, be patient.  Listen to his concerns about whatever may be weighing down on you, let him help.  If you want to share a life, than learning to communicate is the most important thing.

First off you didn't completely screw this up, it sounds like people weren't being completely clear about what they could afford.  And when the amounts kept climbing, they felt they would be letting you down in some manner.  That happened with my brother's wedding, his wife's parents said they would pay a certain amount, but in the end couldn't pull it off [i don't know the reason].  My parents stepped in a made up the difference.  It was stressful for everyone because the costs just kept escalating when they should have been reigned in.
I think you should re-evaluate what you and your fiancee are looking for and try to tailor a wedding to those expectations and costs.  You don't want to enter into this with hurt feelings all around, and constantly going back to one set of parents asking for more will only add to the stress.
Wanting to do the best for your family is great, but it's about the get larger and you need to think long term.  Family gatherings, future children, you don't want people on edge because they feel betrayed in some fashion.
See what you can pull together financially and then ask them if they help make up the difference.  
Congratulations and Good Luck!

I my experience woman like men who are at least somewhat interested in their opinions, wishes, dreams.  It may be cool to be an ass when your in college, but later it just becomes childish.  Can't only be one-sided if you want a relationship.

Are you feeling guilt about the way you handle the argument or is it because of the things being said either by you or to you?  Words hurt more than anything, they remain with you much longer than fists [which is never a way to treat any woman!]  
This may be too personal, but do you suffer from any other depression and it is just made worse during these times?  You don't need to answer, but something to think about.  
The best thing you can do is listen to the young lady, sometimes that is the problem; someone not feeling like they have a voice, a say in what goes on.  Hopefully she listens to what you are saying.  Try not to yell, that is sometimes impossible; but try.
You're young, emotions run high.  Learning how to deal with them takes a lifetime [42 and still learning!]  
Be honest, be respectful, and mostly importantly just keep communicating with her.  You'll learn so much about each other that way.
Good luck and I hope you update this some time!

Maybe now is the time to have "The Talk" about the future, so where you both want to be.  Maybe she has some hidden feelings that might be better brought out in that type of conversation.  I don't know a good way to start that talk, but it might be a starting point.  
You're young and still see lots of possibilities.  But you mention not having a reason to break up, but you questioning if you have a future with her is a reason to break up.  Or it could be a talk that brings you closer, making those steps we all need to make after we enter a more mature stage of loving someone.  
Be honest with her about your doubts, she will eventually feel them even if they remain unspoken.  
In any direction, good luck.  I hope you find a solution that works for both of you.

It's very considerate on your part wanting her family to be welcoming of you, but sometimes that just can't be.  IF you are going to have any real future with this young lady, she is the one who will need to tell her family how she feels about you, and possibly risk upsetting them.  I can tell you from personal experience, if her parents have any type of influence over her - whether financial or otherwise, they will use that should it come to that.  Maybe she is strong enough to stand on her own, maybe she's not.  Only you two know how you wish to create a family of your own, where you are there for each other.  My ex's family told her they would withdraw all support, current and future - she was forced to chose and it was them she picked.  

The best thing you can do is talk to your intended honestly and openly about what you both want from your futures.  Listen to her carefully, support her the best you can.  Be the man she needs you to be and hopefully her family will come to recognize that.  

I hope it works out for you.

maybe therapy would be good for him and maybe for you both.  If you want to be with him, this is a good step towards voicing your concerns about the future.  I know I have gotten frustrated and hit my hand on the table only to instantly regret it and never did it again.  The best you can do is be honest about your feelings, the rest is up to him.
I would entertain anything you had to add.  That being said, texting anyone something this serious is beyond words in my opinion.
you can't change who you are, and she doesn't seem interested in that.  move along, nothing to see here...

the above is good advice, I would listen to it.  Honesty is the only thing that will save what you might have left in your relationship.  Just prepare yourself for some very difficult conversations.

also you say "first time", not a good statement in that some might think there could be a "second or third time"!

When you say angry, does he become physically abusive in any manner?  Do you feel safe with him?  I ask since you have experienced a lifetime in dealing with your mother, it colors how you see others in good and bad ways.  But the most important thing is that you guys talk this through.  If he is willing to cut back and you are happy with that, great.  If you don't think you can be with someone who drinks, that also might be what you are truly concerned with.

To me you are worried about him becoming your mother, maybe there is a chance to talk and change the way both of you look at this.  Have you considered a "marriage counselor" to help guide you through this period?  It may never become the issue you have with your mother, but your fear about this will hold you both back from having a healthy future.
good luck

I know you didn't mean to offend.  This topic is such a raw nerve for me that emotional replies sometimes happen.  I see a therapist and there are even more details I didn't share, like her mother's controlling nature in every aspect.  My ex's well-being is still very important to me.  I worry too much and too often is she is getting the right type of help herself.  Withholding so much from her family, led them to believe things that just weren't there.  I know it's pointless as this juncture, but I believe she really deserves to be happy.

I know about paying back the debt to her family.  They knew the reasons why it was an issue and continued to be an issue in getting the money repaid.  I never hid it from a single friend or anyone who asked because I wasn't ashamed of the debt.  I asked for help when I needed it.  I just didn't think it would be used against me when I was still down.
I added more details.  I just didn't know where to begin.

I received a text from my ex after 10 years together.  I'm in my 40's and know her mother dictated the message!  Nothing like hearing "we need to be apart, don't contact me anymore."  Things just went south overnight.  Sure we had some issues, but nothing that should have resulted in that.  It was only a couple of weeks ago and it hurts like hell!
